# Ushka

> Ushka is an async (ASGI) Python web framework with filesystem routing, built so that insecure code does not run silently. Its main feature, Ushka Guard, makes everything that comes from outside the program (query, form, JSON, headers, cookies, path parameters, and LLM output marked with `guard.llm()`) an `Untrusted` string, and the dangerous sinks (raw HTML responses, the `|safe` filter, `redirect()`, file paths, raw SQL) refuse it with an error that states the risk and the fix. It has a security middleware on by default (CSRF, CSP, HSTS, CORS, trusted hosts), typed parameters and validation without pydantic, `Depends`, WebSockets, SSE, OpenAPI, routes as MCP tools, an async ORM, and `ushka verify`, which attacks your own routes. The core needs only uvicorn, uvloop, httptools, jinja2 and python-multipart. It also has HTML forms and uploads, revocable server-side sessions, internationalisation, SEO tags, an optional PWA and a test client, each described below. Python 3.10+; t-strings on 3.14. Status: 0.8 is in beta (`pip install --pre ushka`); plain `pip install ushka` installs the stable 0.7.

Rules for generating Ushka code:

- Routes: `routes/index.py` is `/`; `routes/users/[user_id].py` is `/users/<user_id>`. Export functions named after the verb: `async def get(request): ...` (also `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `websocket`). Or use decorators on `app = Ushka()`: `@app.get("/path")`.
- Run it with `ushka dev` (reload, debug on) or `ushka run` (production). The app object is `app` in `app.py`; serve it as `app:app`.
- Return a `str`, `dict`/`list` (JSON), `(body, status)` or `(body, status, headers)`, `None` (204), a t-string (3.14, escaped HTML) or `Response`. Raise `HttpNotFound`, `HTTPForbidden`, `HTTPBadRequest` (from `ushka.http.exceptions`) with `message=` as a keyword.
- Type the parameters: `async def get(item_id: int, page: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1)] = 1)`. Bodies are dataclasses or TypedDicts, and `Depends(fn)` injects dependencies. Invalid input answers 422 with every error; for an HTML form use `Annotated[MyDataclass, Form()]` and `@app.post(path, on_invalid=fn)` to draw the form again with `errors.fields` and `errors.values`. An `int`, `UUID`, `Enum` or `Literal` parameter is validated and plain; a `str` stays `Untrusted`. Imports: `from ushka import Query, Header, Cookie, Path, Body, Form, Field, Depends`.
- Never put request values straight into `redirect()`, HTML strings, `|safe`, file paths or raw SQL. Use `from ushka import safe`: `safe.url(v, allow=["/"], default="/")`, `safe.path(v, root)`, `safe.integer(v, min=, max=)`, `safe.choice(v, options)`, `safe.html(v)`. A rejected value answers 400, and so does a NUL byte (`\x00`) anywhere in request text.
- Render HTML with `await render(request, "page.html", {...})` (`from ushka import render`); Jinja2 autoescapes. On 3.14 return `t"<h1>{name}</h1>"`.
- SQL: ORM methods (`await User.filter(name=name)`), `db.text("... :id", id=value)`, or `await db.execute(t"... {value}")`. Not `sqlalchemy.text()` and not f-strings. Several writes that must succeed together go in `async with db.transaction():`. After `await s.rollback()` on your own `db.Session()` the objects are expired; use `await s.rollback(refresh=True)` to keep them readable. Timestamps: `db.DateTime(auto_now_add=True)` (insert) and `db.DateTime(auto_now=True)` (insert and every update); `db.DateTime(timezone=False)` keeps a column without a time zone (`tz=` is an alias). `await db.execute(...)` commits when it runs alone and joins the transaction inside `async with db.transaction():`. A database made by another ORM: `ushka db inspect --write models.py`, then review every `TODO` it leaves (Python-side defaults and missing `ON DELETE` are not in the database), and `ushka db check-models` compares models with the database; to describe an existing table write `__extend_existing__ = True` in the model.
- Mark model output with `guard.llm(text)` (`from ushka import guard`) so it is `Untrusted` too.
- Config: `ushka.toml` (no secrets) < `.env` < env vars `USHKA_<SECTION>_<KEY>` (lists as `a,b`). Secret: `USHKA_APP_SECRET_KEY`. Every setting is listed with its meaning in `ushka.toml` made by `ushka new`, in the Configuration page, and by `ushka config` (add `--describe`); `ushka check` reports unknown keys and wrong types (`csrf = "false"` is a string, not off). Production: `debug = false`, set `[security] allowed_hosts`, run `ushka check --production`.
- Sessions: `request.session["user_id"] = 1` is a signed cookie by default (about 4 KB, and a stolen copy survives logout). For sessions you can end, set `[session] store = "database"` together with `[database] url` (without a database Ushka keeps cookies and warns): then `session.clear()` / `session.revoke()` end it for real, call `session.rotate()` at login, and `await revoke_user_sessions(request, user_id)` (`from ushka.sessions import revoke_user_sessions`) logs a user out everywhere.
- Redirect from anywhere with `raise HTTPRedirect(url)` (`from ushka import HTTPRedirect`): flash messages, session and cookies set before it are kept. The URL still goes through the guard; use `safe.url`. A `Depends` function can stop the request the same way, with `HTTPRedirect(url)` or `raise HTTPResponse(Response(...))`, which is how `login_required` is written.
- Several hostnames in one app: `[routes] hosts = { "api.*" = "routes_api" }` (a folder of route files per host) or `@app.host("api.*").get("/status")`; the host is `request.host`, so combine it with `[security] allowed_hosts`.
- JSON responses serialise `datetime`, `date`, `Decimal` and `UUID` for you; no custom encoder needed.
- Behind a proxy (Caddy, nginx) set `[security] trusted_proxies = ["10.0.0.0/8"]` and read `request.client_ip`, `request.scheme`, `request.host`; `X-Forwarded-*` is trusted only from those addresses, so never parse `X-Forwarded-For` by hand.
- Uploads: take `doc: UploadFile` as a parameter (or `list[UploadFile]`, or `request.files()`), then `doc.save("uploads", extensions=[".png", ".jpg"])`. `filename` and `content_type` are `Untrusted`; a refused extension is a 400. Check `doc.head(8)` magic bytes when the type matters.
- Translations: `[i18n] enable = true`, then `{{ _("Hello") }}` or `{% trans %}` in templates and `from ushka import _, ngettext` in code; catalogs are gettext files in `locale/`, built with `ushka i18n extract` and `ushka i18n compile`.
- Page head: put `{{ seo() }}` in `<head>` instead of `<title>` (override per page with `seo(title=..., description=..., noindex=True)`); `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` are served; set `[seo] url`. For a PWA set `[pwa] enable = true`, add icons, and put `{{ pwa() }}` in `<head>`.
- Tests: `from ushka.testing import TestClient`; `async with TestClient(app) as client: await client.post("/x", json={...})` runs startup and shutdown and keeps cookies.
- Browser writes (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) from another site get 403 (CSRF, no tokens). Allow origins with `[security] csrf_trusted_origins`.
- WebSocket: `async def websocket(ws)` in `routes/`, or `@app.websocket("/ws")`. SSE: return `EventSourceResponse(async_generator)`.
- Expose a route to agents with `@tool(reads=[...], writes=[...])` from `ushka.api.mcp` and `app.enable_mcp()`; sensitive tools need an approver and a token (`USHKA_MCP_TOKEN`).
- Run `ushka verify app:app` to attack your own routes and see what got through; it also probes routes exempt from CSRF (the webhooks), `--as-session uid=1` tests as a logged-in user, and `--cookie NAME=VALUE` / `--header 'Name: value'` (repeatable) send your own credentials (`ushka session --set uid=1` prints a cookie for curl).
- If you hit `UnsafeValueError USHKA-G00x`, apply the `fix` it gives. Do not disable the guard (`[security] taint = false`) and do not use `safe.trust()` without a reason.

## Start

- [Documentation home](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/): where to begin
- [Introduction](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/): the guide by topic
- [Installation](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/install/): pip, extras (orm, postgres, mysql, docs, full), the install script
- [Quickstart](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/quickstart/): a running app in five minutes
- [Project structure](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/project-structure/): what `ushka new` creates
- [Why Ushka changed](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/why-ushka-changed/): purpose and direction
- [Features](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/features/): the short tour

## Guide

- [Routing](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/routing/): file and decorator routes, dynamic segments, hooks
- [Requests and responses](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/requests-responses/): the request object, return values, Response, redirect
- [Validation and typed parameters](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/validation/): types, Query/Header/Body, Depends, 422 errors, OpenAPI
- [Testing](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/testing/): `ushka.testing.TestClient` runs startup/shutdown, keeps cookies, sends json/forms/files, simulates a browser for CSRF
- [Dependency Injection](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/dependency_injection/): request, response and config in a handler
- [Templates](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/templates/): Jinja2, filters, globals, context processors
- [Static files](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/static_files/): the static folder, caching, `app.mount_static`
- [Sessions and cookies](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/sessions/): signed-cookie sessions, revocable server-side sessions (database), rotation, revoking a user everywhere, cookies
- [Uploads](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/uploads/): `UploadFile`, `request.files()`, `save()` with a safe name, limits, validating type and size
- [Internationalisation](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/i18n/): gettext catalogs, `_()` and `{% trans %}`, the language per request from query, cookie or Accept-Language, `ushka i18n extract/compile`
- [SEO](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/seo/): `{{ seo() }}` tags, robots.txt and sitemap.xml ready from `[seo]` in ushka.toml, per-page overrides
- [Progressive Web App](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/pwa/): `[pwa]` in ushka.toml serves the manifest, a conservative service worker and an offline page
- [Flash messages](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/flashing/): one-time messages between requests
- [Error handling](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/error_handling/): HTTP errors, custom pages, debug mode
- [ORM](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/orm/): models, queries, transactions, automatic timestamps, UUID keys, existing databases (`ushka db inspect`), raw SQL, migrations
- [WebSockets and SSE](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/realtime/): sockets, events, streaming
- [Routes as agent tools](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/agents/): MCP, capabilities, human approval
- [Ushka Docs](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/docs/): documentation sites from Markdown, with a cache

## Security

- [Ushka Guard](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/guard/): sources, sinks, sanitisers, error codes USHKA-G001 to G005, limits
- [Security middleware](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/security/): CSRF, headers, CSP (and what it blocks), CORS, trusted hosts, trusted proxies, your own middleware
- [ushka verify](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/verify/): attack your own routes, CSRF-exempt ones included, as an anonymous or a logged-in user
- [Guard on FastAPI, Starlette, Django](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/guard-frameworks/): the same protection in other frameworks

## Run it

- [Configuration](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/configuration/): every setting with its default and meaning (nothing hidden), `ushka config` to inspect them, `ushka new` writes them all, .env and environment variables
- [Deploy](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/deploy/): checklist, Docker, workers, health check, `trusted_proxies` behind Caddy or nginx
- [Performance](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/performance/): uvloop and httptools, idle CPU, benchmarks, how to measure
- [CLI](https://ushka.satela.com.br/docs/guide/cli/): new, dev, run, check, config, session, verify, docs, routes, db, i18n
